summary:
SPAMS (System for Path Approximation on Mars Surface) is a web-based Extravehicular Activity (EVA) mission planner built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map).

We developed a React/Leaflet and Django REST platform covering three Martian research zones—Gale Crater, Jezero Delta, and Melas Chasma—combining real NASA/USGS HiRISE and CTX stereo terrain, DONKI space-weather alerts, REMS/MEDA surface weather, and JPL rover imagery with derived slope, radiation-shielding, and modeled spectral/thermal layers.

SPAMS addresses the challenge by automating multi-stop route planning (A* and Dijkstra) across eight environmental constraints and translatng suit oxygen and battery inputs into realistic buggy transit and on-foot stay-time budgets, ensuring astronauts return to habitat with their chosen safety reserve. A high-contrast HUD mode supports rugged field use, while a one-tap Emergency Comeback button routes astronauts directly back to base using terrain and slope alone.

When humans begin exploring Mars, planning safe traverses and tracking oxygen and battery margins will be part of every surface expedition. By bringing terrain data, route planning, and emergency return together in one interface, SPAMS helps crews stay within safe limits and spend more time on science.
